reason: 'velvety at first' = velutinous in young leaves; the young context (PATO_0000309) carries 'at first'.

fix: 'thinly' before a texture word (thinly coriaceous) is about thickness, not density; it should not be read as degree 'sparsely'. Drop that qualifier or treat it as 'weakly'.
reason: The leaves are chartaceous (papyraceous) or coriaceous, as alternatives within the taxon. Only the qualifier on the second value is a bit off.
'subobtuses' = approximately obtuse, said of the leaf tip. PATO obtuse (blunt end) on the leaf is the usual reading.
'blade subterete' = approximately terete. Putting it on the leaf rather than the lamina is fine for a terete leaf.
'light brownish' = approximately brown. Dropping 'light' does not make it false.
1–5 stems arise from each corm. The corm (PO_0025355) is the container, and the count is right.
3–15 teeth on each side of the leaf lamina, with the 'each side' position recorded.

fix: 'tan' / 'tannish' is a light yellowish brown and belongs under brown, not orange.
reason: Gray is right. 'Tannish' was mapped to orange, but tan is a pale brown.

target: stipe of the fig receptacle (no PO term; reject or use a stalk class)
fix: In 'N cm long stipitate', the length belongs to the stipe (stalk), not to the organ that has it.
reason: The 0–0.8 cm is the length of the receptacle's stipe. The receptacle itself is 0.8–1.5 cm across.
The inflorescence is 4–6-flowered: 4–6 flowers per inflorescence.
The culms are slightly fibrillose at the base, so a fibrous texture on the stem base matches what the flora says (the fibres probably come from the basal sheaths).
For prostrate plants, FNA gives height × spread. The width of 0.3–2(–2.5) dm converts correctly to 3–20(–25) cm.

fix: 'others' after 'margin entire on lower leaves' means the remaining (upper) leaves, and that position must be kept.
reason: The lower leaves have entire margins. Only the other leaves have 3–5 teeth per side, and the annotation leaves that limit out.
'Baccate' = berry-like, so the fruit is fleshy.
'Monadelphous' = stamens united by their filaments into one group. Connate is the right parent, since FLOPO has diadelphous but no monadelphous class.
The stem leaves are erect-appressed when dry, and the dried condition is recorded.
The ovary is shortly stipitate (on a short stalk).

target: position: upper part of the involucral bract
fix: 'dans la partie supérieure' ('in the upper part') limits the quality to that part of the organ and must fill the position slot.
reason: The venation is reticulate only in the upper part of the involucral bracts. Without that, the statement reads as if the whole bract were reticulate.
The style is longer than the stamens.
'Many flowered' inflorescence = flowers present in a large number, within the inflorescence.

target: hyalodermis (outer cortical cell layer of the moss stem; no PO term; reject)
fix: In '<tissue> large' after 'Stems', 'large' belongs to the named tissue or its cells, not to the stem.
reason: 'Large' describes the hyalodermis cells. The stem itself is 0.3–1 cm.
There are 5 leaflets.

fix: 'largest X, blade a–b cm' gives the size of the largest member only. Record it as a maximum or keep the 'largest' qualifier.
reason: 12–17 cm is the blade length of the largest sterile pinna, not of every pinna.
The terminal buds are glabrous, and the 'terminal' context is recorded.

fix: Margin-shape words (crenate, serrate, dentate) said of a leaf belong on the leaf margin.
reason: 'Irregularly crenate-serrate' describes the margin of the leaves. Reading it as a continuum from crenate to serrate is fine.
The lower bracts are about 8 mm wide, and the 'lower' position is recorded.
The habit is prostrate, scrambling (mapped to climbing by the reviewed rule) or ascending.
'Marge non denticulée' = the petal margin is not toothed.
The petiole is 1–2 cm long.
The flowers are yellow or purplish.
